questions.question: Why does precision count only suggested results?
options: Review results are too slow to count.
To make the number look better.
Sending a hard case to review is correct behaviour, not a wrong answer.
questions.explanation: Precision asks "when the service commits to an answer, is it right?". Review cases are measured separately by the review rate.

questions.question: Why use the 95th percentile instead of the average for latency?
options: Averages hide the slow calls that people notice.
questions.explanation: One very slow call can hide behind many fast ones in an average. The 95th percentile shows what nearly every caller experiences.

questions.question: Which statement is a measurable requirement?
options: At most 30% of companies in the labelled sample need review.
The service should rarely be wrong.
questions.explanation: It names the indicator, the target, and where it is measured. The others cannot be checked.
